newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent basis surges on refiner buying.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent basis surges on refiner buying.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline and diesel fuel differentials firmed on Wednesday during a heavy round of refiner buying led by major oil companies, traders said.
"There's some big volumes getting done. It looks like refiner buying to cover ahead of maintenance," one Chicago-area trader said.
The run-up also was fueled by a bullish 481,000 barrel draw in gasoline stocks last week that left inventories 2.1 million barrels below the same week last year, traders said.

Refineries in the region were operated at 94.6 percent of capacity last week, down 0.1 percentage points from the prior week. Distillate stocks in the region were drawn down 1 million barrels last week but remained 435,000 barrels ahead of the same week last year, API said.
Group Three low sulphur diesel for late-January deliveries was talked 1.25/1.00 cent a gallon under NYMEX February heating oil, with high suphur 3.50 cents under.
Chicago low sulphur diesel for February deliveries firmed one cent a gallon to 0.75/0.50 cent a gallon under NYMEX March heating oil, with high sulphur 1.75 cents under.
Prompt unleaded gasoline was bid 1.50 cents under NYMEX February unleaded in Group Three and remained 0.75 cent under NYMEX March unleaded in Chicago.
